title: Upward Technologies vs Apollo.io
content_html:
Upward Technologies vs Apollo.io

Upward Technologies vs Apollo.io serve different needs in the go-to-market space. Apollo.io is built for sales teams running outbound campaigns across email, LinkedIn, calls and SMS, with a B2B contact database and lead enrichment at its core. Upward Technologies builds custom software, automation and AI agents for operations, finance and IT teams whose repetitive work spans invoicing, data entry, document processing and integrations between systems. If your team is running outbound sales campaigns, Apollo.io is the specialist. If your team loses hours to manual work across multiple tools that do not fit how you work, Upward Technologies is the better fit.

What Apollo.io is good at

Apollo.io combines a B2B database with campaign automation across multiple channels. According to its website, it offers email accuracy on contact data, waterfall enrichment from multiple data sources to fill gaps in records, and the ability to bring together data from a customer's CRM, data warehouse and call recordings into one place.

The platform runs automated campaigns across email, LinkedIn, calls, WhatsApp and SMS from one workflow, and integrates with CRMs including HubSpot, Salesforce and Pipedrive. It also connects to VoIP tools Aircall and Ringover, and supports Google, Microsoft and SMTP mailboxes for sending. Apollo.io offers integrations across the platform, and developers can connect Apollo to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any Model Context Protocol (MCP) client. Users can sign up free without a credit card, and the platform uses a credit system for usage.

If your team's main job is finding and reaching prospects at scale, Apollo.io is a mature, focused tool built exactly for that.

What Upward Technologies does differently

Upward Technologies builds custom software, automation and AI agents around the way a team already works. Rather than starting with a pre-built platform, a three-week paid scoping phase maps your exact processes before anything is built. The scoping phase ends with a document the client could take to another supplier, so both sides know exactly what will be built and why.

After scoping, Upward Technologies builds the software and hosts and runs it. The company also builds AI agents for repetitive work such as document processing, data entry and answering questions from company documents. Where Apollo.io is a SaaS tool you configure, Upward Technologies is a builder and operator of custom software tailored to your process.

Upward Technologies also offers standalone products for specific needs. Reach is B2B outreach software that drafts and sequences messages for approval before sending, so teams keep control over personalization. For teams that need outreach as part of a larger workflow (for example, prospect research feeds into document generation and then into e-signature), custom software can integrate all three steps into one system.

Which one should you pick

Pick Apollo.io if: your team runs outbound sales campaigns and needs a database of verified B2B contacts, lead enrichment, and multi-channel campaign automation. Apollo.io is purpose-built for this and scales well. It also suits teams that want to start quickly with a pre-built platform and configure it themselves.

Pick Upward Technologies if: your team's manual work spans multiple processes (not just outreach), or your outreach is part of a larger workflow that existing tools do not connect. For example, if prospect research, quote generation, e-signature and follow-up all happen in your team's week, custom software can integrate all of them so data enters once. Upward Technologies also suits teams that need outreach with stronger control over personalization before messages go out, or teams whose compliance or data requirements mean software must run on your own hardware or hosted servers in the Netherlands.

Pick both if: your team runs outreach campaigns (Apollo.io) but also has manual work outside of campaigns that needs automation. Many teams use Apollo.io for outbound and then build custom software to connect the results back into finance, operations or support workflows.

FAQ

What is the difference between Apollo.io and Reach?

Apollo.io is a full outbound platform with a B2B database, lead enrichment, and multi-channel campaign automation. Reach is Upward Technologies's B2B outreach product that drafts and sequences messages for a person to approve before sending, so teams keep control over personalization and tone. Reach suits teams that want to automate the repetitive parts of outreach (drafting, scheduling) but keep the relationship-building parts (approval, customization) in human hands. If you also need a contact database and lead enrichment, Apollo.io is the better fit on its own.

Can Upward Technologies integrate with Apollo.io?

Yes. Upward Technologies builds custom software that can pull data from Apollo.io via its API and route it into your other systems (CRM, finance, support). This suits teams that use Apollo.io for campaigns but need the results to flow into custom workflows in operations or finance.

Does Upward Technologies build outreach software?

Upward Technologies offers Reach, a B2B outreach product, and also builds custom software for teams whose outreach is part of a larger workflow. For teams that need outreach as a standalone tool, Apollo.io is the stronger choice because it includes a contact database and lead enrichment. For teams that need outreach integrated with document generation, e-signature, or CRM workflows, custom software is often the better fit.

Can I move from Apollo.io to Upward Technologies?

Yes. Apollo.io exports your contacts and campaign data. Upward Technologies can use that data to build custom software that connects outreach to your other processes. The three-week scoping phase would map how outreach fits into your larger workflow and whether a custom solution makes sense.

Is Apollo.io better for small sales teams?

Apollo.io is built for sales teams running campaigns, regardless of size. It starts free and scales with usage. If your team is small and only does outreach, Apollo.io is a good fit. If your small team also does other manual work (invoicing, data entry, document processing), custom software that integrates all of it might save more time than running separate tools.

What does the three-week scoping phase cover?

The scoping phase is a paid engagement that maps your current process, identifies which steps repeat, which steps need a human decision, and which steps could be automated or integrated. It ends with a document that describes the software to be built and a go or no-go decision. The document can be taken to another supplier if you choose. This phase settles whether custom software makes sense before any code is written.
